references.text: Jacob gave Joseph a special coat as a sign of favoritism. Now Joseph himself gives clothes to his brothers, with special attention to Benjamin—a parallel to the father's favoritism.

Benjamin received five times as much food as his other brothers at Joseph's table, reflecting the special relationship between Joseph and Benjamin—here Benjamin also receives five changes of clothing and 300 silver pieces.
Joseph also sent gifts to his father Jacob, as part of his generosity when he revealed his identity and reconciled with his brothers.
Naaman took along changes of clothing (חֲלִפוֹת) as gifts, the same word used for the changes of clothing Joseph gave to his brothers.
Samson promised 30 changes of clothing (חֲלִפוֹת שְׂמָלוֹת) as a prize—the same expression used for the gifts Joseph gave to his brothers.
The gift to Benjamin in 45:22 is the direct consequence and confirmation of his innocence and special role, as revealed in 44:12.
